correctness.rationale: The group law a,b was materialized on all 24 permutations. For identity words of length>24, 25 prefix positions force an identity subword of length<=24, so induction decomposes the Parikh vector into identity vectors from bounded length. The exact P_ij right-multiplication DP through total length24 independently reconstructs all 325 Parikh coordinates and agrees with the proposed five generator monoid; generator irredundancy and its even/odd modulus-4 membership normal form follow from nonnegative semigroup bounds. Periodic folding (i mod 4 beyond 9, j mod 2 beyond 3) gives 65 reachable canonical count states. Independently computing the complete DFA successor partition yields exactly 44 pairwise distinguishable right-congruence classes, with 33 classes size1, nine size2 and two size7. The finite group reduction and automaton partition exhaust all infinite words, unlike an arbitrary truncated simulation.
residual_risks: The 24-word cutoff is justified by prefix pigeonhole; the first 100 lengths alone would not establish it.

value.rationale: S4 with a 4-cycle and transposition is a standard smallest nonabelian symmetric-group test case. The exact five primitive identity-count vectors and 44-class minimal recognizer are independently useful sharp benchmarks for commutative closure/state complexity beyond qualitative regularity and broad bounds. The evidence is a complete natural exact invariant, not an arbitrary choice of finite sample.
residual_risks: No claim for all S_n or arbitrary generating sets; a single finite benchmark has limited generality and future reuse remains an informed prospect.

final_claim: For positive letters a=(0 1 2 3) and b=(0 1) generating S4, identity-product word language W, the Parikh monoid is minimally generated by (0,2),(4,0),(3,3),(6,4),(9,3), and its commutative closure has exactly 44 states in a complete minimal DFA.
limitations: Complete deterministic automata including rejecting states; group identity and a 4-point stabilizer language must not be conflated.
